ety.text: From Proto-Common Turkic *bēšik, from Proto-Turkic *bẹĺčig. See also Turkish beşik.

Acronym of бе́ло-си́не-кра́сный (bélo-síne-krásnyj), referring to the white-blue-red colours/colors of the Russian flag. This acronym was used before the establishment of the Soviet Union, during Tsarist times.

ety.text: Of Proto-Slavic origin, the exact etymology is uncertain. A number of hypotheses have been proposed. * Perhaps related to ключ (ključ, “spring”), ключеви́на (ključevína, “swamp fed by springs”), i.e. “swamp berry”. Chernykh favors this explanation; Shansky considers it unconvincing. * Perhaps related to клю́кать (kljúkatʹ, “to slurp”) and Serbo-Croatian кљук (“grape must”), of onomatopoeic origin, referring to the sound of berries being juiced; Vasmer lists this hypothesis first. * Perhaps derived via metathesis from *клювка (compare Serbo-Croatian кљувка) and thus from клюв (kljuv, “beak”),…

s.g: of the yellowish-red colour/color of freshly felled pine

ety.text: From the noun конда (konda), from earlier ко́нга (kónga), from Finnish honka (“large, straight pine tree”).
